critical_issues.what:
The corrected mechanic was added to structured_output.repo_patterns.idempotency_helper (line 33) and to the top-level summary — both correctly describe `${operationName}:${randomUUID()}` per-call distinct keys. However, MANY supporting fields throughout the file still propagate the original WRONG mental model: that testFetch's body-fingerprint would 'collapse' identical-body POSTs into a same-key replay. Examples of stale text still present:
  - evidence[1] (line 5): 'auto-applies createIdempotencyHeaders ... using body sha256 fingerprint' (without correcting that the unique key is randomUUID, not the body hash)
  - inferences[0] (line 18): 'specs that retry the SAME body (S17 replay, S22 dead-write replay) will get the SAME key automatically' — this is the EXACT opposite of the truth
  - inferences[1] (line 19): 'testFetch normally auto-fingerprints' as if override is required to defeat collapse
  - S15 line 936: 'collapsing them into a same-key replay' — wrong
  - S15 line 949: helper described as 'bypass the auto-fingerprint' — wrong framing
  - S17 line 1052: 'relying on testFetch's body-fingerprint would give same key auto-replay' — wrong
  - S27 line 1576/1599: '...to defeat testFetch's auto-fingerprint replay' — wrong
  - review_focus line 1787 and notes_for_phase_5 line 1795: both still tell Phase 5 the wrong default behavior

A literal-minded Phase 5 reading inferences[0] or notes_for_phase_5[0] will build the wrong mental model and may write code (e.g. raw http bypass for distinct-key cases) that is unnecessary, or skip explicit-key overrides for same-key replays thinking testFetch already does it.
critical_issues.fix:
Do a find/replace pass to remove the false 'collapse' / 'auto-fingerprint replay' framing. Concretely:
  1. evidence[1] symbol field: replace 'using body sha256 fingerprint' with 'using `${operationName}:${randomUUID()}` per call (body sha256 is namespace only, not the unique key)'
  2. inferences[0]: rewrite to 'testFetch's createIdempotencyHeaders assigns DISTINCT random keys per call by default. Specs that intend SAME-KEY REPLAY (S17 confirm replay, S18 bulk-confirm replay, S19 complete replay, S22 dead-write replay) MUST explicitly set options.headers["Idempotency-Key"]=K1 on BOTH calls — otherwise each call gets a fresh randomUUID and the assertion target (idempotent no-op) is not exercised. Specs that intend DISTINCT-KEY parallel (S15, S24, S27) can rely on the default; explicit keys are belt-and-suspenders only.'
  3. inferences[1]: drop 'testFetch normally auto-fingerprints' — replace with 'testFetch's default already gives distinct random keys, but specs should still pass explicit Idempotency-Keys to make the intent unambiguous in the test source.'
  4. S15 interaction_plan line 907: change 'so the auto-fingerprint does not collapse them into a single replay' to 'making the distinct-key intent explicit (testFetch defaults to randomUUID per call but explicit keys document the test intent)'
  5. S15 flakiness_risks line 936: change to 'testFetch defaults to a per-call randomUUID Idempotency-Key (no body-based collapse), but Phase 5 should still pass explicit distinct keys to make the BR-8b test intent obvious from the spec source.'
  6. S15 new_helpers_recommended line 949: change 'wrapper that sets Idempotency-Key explicitly to bypass the auto-fingerprint' to 'wrapper that sets a specified Idempotency-Key explicitly (testFetch's default is randomUUID; this helper makes the key choice visible at the call site).'
  7. S17 interaction_plan line 1025: change 'override the auto-fingerprint' to 'forced same-key replay; without this explicit header testFetch would assign a fresh randomUUID and the replay would be a different idempotency key entirely.'
  8. S17 flakiness_risks line 1052: rewrite to 'Phase 5 MUST explicitly set Idempotency-Key='K1' on BOTH POSTs — testFetch's default randomUUID would give DIFFERENT keys, so without the override the second call would NOT replay the first (the wrong assertion target).'
  9. S17 new_helpers_recommended line 1064: change 'wrapper bypassing the auto-fingerprint' to 'wrapper that sets an explicit Idempotency-Key (the default randomUUID would NOT replay).'
  10. S27 interaction_plan line 1576: drop 'to defeat testFetch's auto-fingerprint replay' — replace with '(testFetch's default randomUUID would already give distinct keys; explicit keys make the intent visible).'
  11. S27 flakiness_risks line 1599: rewrite to 'Phase 5 should pass explicit distinct Idempotency-Keys to make the natural-retry intent visible in the spec; the default would also give distinct keys but readers cannot tell from the source.'
  12. review_focus[5] line 1787: rewrite to 'Verify same-key replay specs (S17, S18, S19) explicitly set options.headers[Idempotency-Key]=K1 on BOTH calls. Verify distinct-key specs (S15, S22, S24, S27) make the distinct-key intent visible at the call site.'
  13. notes_for_phase_5[0] line 1795: rewrite to 'testFetch auto-applies createIdempotencyHeaders for non-GET methods; the auto key is `${operationName}:${randomUUID()}` per call (distinct random keys by default). Same-key replay (S17/S18/S19) REQUIRES explicit options.headers[Idempotency-Key]=K1 on both calls. Distinct-key parallel (S15/S24/S27) can rely on default but should still pass explicit keys for source-level clarity.'

Note: the actual interaction_plan steps that say 'POST ... with explicit Idempotency-Key=K1' are CORRECT — the operational guidance is right, only the surrounding rationale text propagates the wrong mental model.
